title: 12 Easy Crochet Cardigan Patterns for Beginners: Modern, Wearable Styles
excerpt: Choose your first cardigan from 12 beginner-friendly crochet patterns, with rectangles, cocoon and hexagon shapes, granny squares, lace, videos and practical fit tips.

featuredImage.alt: Four beginner-friendly crochet cardigan styles in neutral, granny-square, hexagon and lace designs
featuredImage.caption: Original AI-generated feature illustration for the beginner cardigan roundup.

contentHtml:
Want to crochet your first cardigan but feel unsure about sizing, sleeves or joining pieces? Start with a design whose construction makes sense to you. A cardigan made from rectangles is often easier to plan than a fitted garment; a cocoon or hexagon cardigan reduces shaping; and granny-square styles let you work one small motif at a time.

About the pictures: the images in this guide are original AI-generated style illustrations, not photos of the patterns made by their designers. They help you compare silhouettes and color ideas. Use each linked source for the accurate pattern, materials, gauge, measurements, size range and current access terms.

Why these styles feel current: Pinterest’s official Summer 2026 trend report highlights rising interest in patchwork jackets and handmade, one-of-a-kind details. It does not report a specific increase for crochet cardigans, so this is a style cue rather than a cardigan search-volume claim. Granny squares, modular panels and thoughtful color placement translate that visual direction into beginner-friendly crochet projects. See Pinterest’s Summer 2026 trend report.

For a broader comparison across skill levels, visit our 15 free crochet cardigan patterns roundup. If you want to follow one garment from materials through finishing, our Wetherby Crop Cardigan guide and Autumn Brioche Cardigan guide offer more detailed make-along support.

Choose your first cardigan by construction

If this is your priority… Try this construction Why it can feel approachable
Few new techniques Rectangles or simple panels Practice rows, measuring and seaming
Less shaping Cocoon or hexagon Build the body from one large piece or two repeated shapes
Flexible, portable crochet Granny squares Work small motifs in short sessions, then assemble
Lightweight layering Repeating lace stitch Learn one open stitch repeat and check drape with a swatch

Quick level guide: “Beginner” assumes you can make chains and basic stitches. “Confident beginner” means you may need to learn one extra skill, such as gauge, joining squares, a V-stitch or shaping a hexagon. None of the patterns below is a promise of instant results; use the source’s own skill notes and take your time with fit.

12 easy crochet cardigan patterns for beginners

1. The Everyday Easy Crochet Cardigan

Pattern format: Free written pattern with step-by-step photos and stitch videos; optional ad-free PDF.
Designer: Yippie Yarn Yay. Level: Absolute beginner.

If your biggest worry is getting stuck halfway through a garment, this is the gentlest place to start. The designer keeps the stitch vocabulary to single crochet and double crochet and includes photo guidance plus video help for the stitches. That makes it easier to focus on measuring and assembling the cardigan instead of learning several new textures at once. Open the pattern first to check its size chart and yarn quantities, then make the recommended swatch; a simple stitch can still produce a cardigan that is too wide or too short if tension changes.

View the free pattern and PDF options

2. Simple Crochet Cardigan by Viv Crochets

Pattern format: Free written pattern and video tutorial.
Designer: Viv Crochets. Level: Beginner, according to the designer.

This drop-shoulder cardigan keeps the stitch plan simple: the designer uses one main stitch throughout and works the garment in three pieces rather than five. The page includes a free written pattern and video tutorial, plus notes explaining how to adjust the sample dimensions. The listed sample is a small adult size, so compare the pattern’s measurements with your preferred fit before starting. You will still need to make ribbed edges and sew the panels together, but the repeat itself stays straightforward.

Open the free pattern and video tutorial

3. Easy Rectangle Cardigan

Pattern format: Free written pattern with video tutorial; printable PDF is optional.
Designer: Delia Creates. Level: Beginner.

This cardigan is built from simple rectangular pieces, so the construction is easy to picture before you pick up the hook. Rectangle construction is a good first-garment route for people who already know a basic stitch and want to practise measuring, seaming and finishing. The source includes sizes XXS–XXL and a video tutorial. Work a swatch in the stitch used by the pattern and block it if the designer recommends it; matching the rectangle dimensions is what makes the sleeves and body line up cleanly.

View the free pattern and PDF options

4. Fireside Cardigan with Pockets

Pattern format: Free pattern on the blog; optional paid ad-free PDF with photo tutorials and schematic.
Designer: A Crocheted Simplicity. Level: Beginner-friendly; read the construction notes first.

Want a cardigan that feels useful right away? The Fireside pattern pairs a relaxed shape with tapered sleeves and inset pockets. The designer describes it as a beginner-friendly, one-piece construction and provides sizes from XS through 5X. Because pockets and ribbing add finishing steps, it is a satisfying next project after you feel comfortable with basic rows. The blog pattern is free to read, while the printable PDF is an optional purchase; check the current page for yarn amounts and gauge.

View the free pattern and PDF options

5. Cocoon Cardigan from a C2C Square

Pattern format: Free pattern and video tutorial; printable PDF may be offered separately.
Designer: HanJan Crochet. Level: Beginner-friendly if you know the basic C2C increase.

This cocoon-style layer is made from a square worked corner to corner, then shaped with a small number of seams. The construction is appealing if sleeves and fitted armholes feel intimidating: the loose silhouette is created by folding and joining the fabric. The source page gives adult sizes XS–5XL and has a video tutorial. C2C uses increases and decreases, so practise that repeat on a small swatch first and measure the square as you go.

View the free pattern and PDF options

6. Short-Sleeve Cardigan in Simple Panels

Pattern format: Free written pattern and video tutorial.
Designer: Winding Road Crochet. Level: Beginner to confident beginner.

A short-sleeved cardigan uses less yarn and finishes faster than a long-sleeved layer, which makes it a practical warm-weather project. This design is assembled from two rectangles and two squares, giving you a manageable way to practise joining pieces. The source page includes a free pattern and video; follow its schematic for the dimensions of each panel. Short sleeves do not remove the need for fit checks, so compare the body width and arm opening with a garment you own before seaming.

Open the pattern and video tutorial

7. Polka Crop Cardigan

Pattern format: Free pattern and video tutorial; check source for current PDF options.
Designer: The Knotty Lace. Level: Beginner-friendly per designer.

The cropped length and small bobble details give this cardigan a playful look while keeping the body shape straightforward. The creator provides a video and says the sizing runs from children through adult 5XL, so this may work well for a family project or a personalized gift. Bobbles require a little extra attention, but the tutorial lets you see how they are formed. Check the designer’s gauge and finished measurements, especially if you plan to wear it over a dress or high-waisted outfit.

View the free pattern and PDF options

8. Elowen Hexagon Cardigan

Pattern format: Free pattern and full video tutorial.
Designer: Off the Beaten Hook. Level: Beginner-friendly; gauge swatch recommended.

Two hexagons fold into the body and sleeves of this relaxed cardigan, which keeps the main construction memorable: make two matching shapes, fold, join, then finish the edges. The designer provides a free written pattern and a full video. The pattern includes a size chart and stresses checking gauge, particularly after blocking. It is an approachable way to try a more garment-like silhouette without separately shaping a front, back and two sleeves.

Open the pattern and video tutorial

9. Easy One-Stitch Lace Cardigan

Pattern format: Free written pattern and video; optional ad-free printable pattern.
Designer: The Knotty Lace. Level: Beginner-approachable if you can make US double crochet.

This airy layer uses a repeating V-stitch, made from double crochet stitches and a chain space. Repetition helps beginners settle into a rhythm, while the open fabric gives the cardigan a light, draped finish. The creator describes the pattern as beginner-approachable and includes a video. Open the source to confirm the size range and gauge before selecting yarn; lace fabric stretches and drapes differently from a dense cardigan, so a swatch is especially useful.

Open the pattern and video tutorial

10. Modern Granny Square Cardigan

Pattern format: Free written pattern for subscribers plus detailed video; ad-free PDF may be available.
Designer: HanJan Crochet. Level: Confident beginner; granny-square experience helps.

This modern square-based design adds a more graphic, hand-assembled look to the cardigan styles appearing in current patchwork-inspired fashion. It is a worthwhile step after you can make consistent squares and are ready to join panels neatly. The designer page includes materials, a detailed video and free written pattern access for blog subscribers. The construction is more involved than a simple rectangle, so block the motifs to equal dimensions before assembly and check the source for the cardigan’s exact size and yarn requirements.

View the free pattern and PDF options

11. Granny Square Kimono Cardigan

Pattern format: Free step-by-step pattern and video tutorial.
Designer: The Knotty Lace. Level: Confident beginner.

This long kimono-shaped layer lets the granny squares create the visual interest, while the open front and generous sleeves keep fitting simple. It is a good project if you enjoy making small motifs in batches and want a more flowing silhouette than a cropped cardigan. The creator provides written instructions and a video tutorial. Before crocheting a full set of motifs, make one square and check the finished measurement against the pattern; consistent square size makes the later joining much easier.

Open the pattern and video tutorial

12. Grateful + Thankful Granny Cardigan

Pattern format: Free pattern and video tutorial; verify current size and yarn notes on source.
Designer: Hayhay Crochet. Level: Confident beginner; a good next project after your first cardigan.

This boxy, cropped cardigan brings several granny-square motifs together with a ribbed edge and optional buttons. The designer’s page includes a video and detailed size guidance, with sizes listed through 4XL. It takes more planning and joining than a one-piece cardigan, but the repeated square construction can make the work feel approachable. Lay out the motifs before sewing them together to plan the color order and catch any size mismatch early.

How to get a better fit on your first cardigan

Before ordering yarn, take a cardigan from your closet that fits the way you want this one to fit. Measure its chest width, body length and sleeve length while it is laid flat. Compare those numbers with the finished measurements in the crochet pattern; garment size labels vary, and “oversized” does not tell you exactly how much ease the designer built in.

  • Make the gauge swatch. Use the yarn, hook and stitch specified by the pattern. Wash or block the swatch if the instructions call for it, then measure again.
  • Choose yarn for drape. A soft DK or worsted yarn may suit an everyday cardigan, but fiber and weight affect warmth, stretch and weight. Follow the recommended category and yardage.
  • Check the pattern terminology. US and UK stitch names differ. Confirm which terms the designer uses before you begin.
  • Mark pieces as you go. Label matching fronts, sleeves and motifs so they do not get confused during assembly.
  • Try it on before the final seams. Pin panels together or use removable stitch markers, then check the body width and sleeve opening before sewing permanently.
  • Plan colors with small samples. For patchwork or granny-square styles, arrange a few finished motifs on the floor before making the whole set. A photo of the layout helps keep the color balance consistent.

Frequently asked questions

What is the easiest crochet cardigan construction for a beginner?

Many beginners find a rectangle or a few simple panels easiest to understand because the pieces are straightforward to measure. If you prefer fewer seams, a cocoon or hexagon construction can be a good next choice, especially when the pattern includes a full video.

Can I crochet a cardigan without making a gauge swatch?

You can, but it makes fit less predictable. Even a small difference in stitch width can change a cardigan’s chest measurement by several inches. A swatch is especially valuable for wearable garments, granny-square motifs and open lace stitches.

Are these patterns all free?

Most offer free instructions on the designer’s site or a free tutorial; some also offer an optional paid, ad-free PDF. Access terms can change, so check the linked page before you start or purchase.

Which cardigan style is best for a warm-weather layer?

A short-sleeved cardigan, cropped style or open lace design uses a lighter silhouette. Choose cotton or another breathable yarn only if it matches the pattern’s gauge and drape recommendations.

Can I change the length or sleeves?

Often, but first check whether the designer gives modification notes. Adding rows or rounds changes yarn use and may affect how the panels join. Make one adjustment at a time and measure the garment as you work.

Pick the project that will keep you crocheting

If you want the simplest start, choose a basic-stitch or rectangle pattern. If a modern patchwork look is what caught your eye, start with a small granny-square project and plan the layout before assembly. If you learn best by watching, select one of the patterns with a full video and work along at your own pace.

Save the pattern page, check its size and yarn notes, and complete a swatch before beginning the main pieces. Then explore the rest of our Crochet Cardigan Pattern collection for more wearable ideas and step-by-step guides.
